newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer says fundraising not tied to Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: Placer says fundraising not tied to Bre-X.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Thursday that its plan to raise more than US$300 million from asset sales and preferred securities was not connected to its efforts to strike a deal with Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
"It's not related at all to Busang," said Placer spokesman Hugh Leggatt, referring to Bre-X's massive gold field in Indonesia.

Placer has asked the Indonesian government to allow it to make a competing offer for Bre-X, which is in advanced discussions on a joint venture with Barrick Gold Corp at the direction of the Indonesian government.
Leggatt said the package of steps was intended to fuel growth at the gold company by sharpening its focus on high-quality gold production.

Placer plans to sell its Sigma and Kiena mines in Quebec, both of which were small. Sigma last year produced 78,000 ounces of gold at an average cash cost of US$367 an ounce and had reserves of 448,000 ounces. Kiena produced 87,000 ounces at US$238 an ounce and had reserves of 570,000 ounces.
Sigma was carried on Placer's books at a value of US$18 million and Kiena US$78 million. "We don't regard them as core gold operations," Leggatt said.
Placer also plans to sell its Endako molybdenum mine and scale back mining at its Detour Lake mine to focus on exploration of a promising zone there.

Work is being stopped at Paymaster, a property adjoining Placer's Dome mine that hosted a mine until it was abandoned in the 1960s. Placer has been exploring the possibility of re-opening the mine, but determined it was not viabile,
It is also plans to issue US$300 million in preferred securities in the United States for terms of up to 49 years.
Leggatt said Placer was intent on upgrading the quality of its operations. "We want to focus more on high-quality production from low-cost mines with long life," he said.
